# Guideline 3 - Build conflict through roleplay Conflict makes great stories, and we want plenty of it. What we ask is that it grows out of roleplay, not out of a wish to win. [textlink="Roleplay Rule 11 - Follow reasonable escalation" link="RuleR11"] is the rule that gets enforced; this guideline is the spirit we would like to see on top of it.
- Start with words. Arguments, threats, bargaining and social pressure are all part of the story, long before anyone throws a punch. - Let the other side respond. Match their level and give them room to back down, answer back or make things worse. - Look for a way out where it makes sense. Someone watching your whole round should never think your goal was to find a fight. - Have a clear in-character reason before you reach for [color=#ff0000]lethal force[/color]. "They annoyed me" or "they were in my way" is not enough. - Permanent death should be rare, and only reached when the other side took the conflict there.
Antagonists have more freedom under Rule 11, but the best antagonist moments are built with roleplay too: pressure, manipulation and tension before the violence.
## Examples Good: - A dispute over a workspace starts with an argument, then a shove, then a fistfight, each step a response to the other person. - As security, you talk to a suspect first, warn them, then use non-lethals when they resist. - As an antagonist, you manipulate and pressure a target over several minutes before your plan turns violent.
Not what we are looking for: - Pulling a weapon and going lethal over a verbal insult. - "Winning" a small argument by immediately critting the other person. - Treating every round as an excuse to go looking for fights. - As an antagonist, gibbing a random bystander at round start with no roleplay behind it.
